title: Midday ops docket — Omar oncall notes
content:
Midday ops docket — scratchpad and handoff notes
Owner: Omar Khan (oncall)
Date: 2026-03-24
Shift: 08:00–16:00 PT (midday)

Summary / high-level
- Woke to one major page early morning (02:13 PT): high p95/p99 latency for model-serving cluster in eu-west-1 (svc-model-v2).
- Pager: automated alert from latency-slo-service (alert id latency-slo-02).
- Mitigation: rolled back canary job that introduced cache-warmup, temporarily increased replica count for serving pool, cleared some prefix caches, latencies returned to baseline by 03:05 PT.
- Root cause hypothesis: cache-warmup job (new canary) caused heavy memory churn and constant cache invalidation, forcing frequent KV cache rebuilds and long GC pauses on 3 hosts.
- Follow-up actions and runbook TODOs below.

Timeline (brief)
- 02:13 PT: Pager triggered (p99 > 1.5s for 5m). Pager included raw traces link and example request ids.
- 02:18 PT: Confirmed spiky host-level memory + swap use on host-12, host-14, host-19 (eu-west-1).
- 02:25 PT: Noted increased OOM-killer events in dmesg on host-14.
- 02:30 PT: Identified a recent deploy: jobs/cache-warmup:tag-2026-03-24-canary (by CI pipeline).
- 02:35 PT: Scaled serving pool from 12->18 (quick horizontal scale) while investigating.
- 02:45 PT: Rolled back canary job to previous tag.
- 03:05 PT: Latency returned to expected distribution (p99 ~ 230ms).
- 04:30 PT: Post-incident verification, no recurrence for 60m.

Notes / commands run (for personal reference)
- kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=svc-model-v2 -o wide -> spotted 3 pods with OOM restarts
- journalctl -u kubelet | grep "OOM"
- curl -s "https://tracing.redwood.com/trace?q=request_id:abc123" -> heavy KV-cache misses shown

Immediate mitigations taken (repro steps to avoid repeat during shift)
- Rolled back canary for jobs/cache-warmup (CI rollback).
- Temporary scale-up of serving pool to absorb in-flight work.
- Manual cache prefix purge for the affected prefix to reduce rebuild load.
- Enabled graceful-fallback routing for tiered-models so low-tier can handle burst until root cause addressed.

Root cause analysis (notes, tentative)
- The new warmup job implemented aggressive parallel prefetch without concurrency limits. It appears to have flooded the local node memory, triggering frequent GC/OOM and evictions.
- The serving runtime reacts poorly when KV-cache is continuously rebuilding (lock contention + long-tail latencies).
- Canary rollout did not have a mem-usage sensor/alert; only latency alerts fired (too late).

Owner-assigned follow-ups (actionable)
- ACTION-1: Update cache-warmup job to include concurrency throttle + memory cap. Owner: Platform Eng (Lena Park). Due: 2026-03-26. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678
- ACTION-2: Add preflight Canary health check for mem usage + OOM events to deployment pipeline. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Samir Rao). Due: 2026-04-02. Jira: SRE-4123
- ACTION-3: Harden runbook 'svc-model-v2 high-latency' with clear steps for identifying cache-warmup impact (grep dmesg, check job labels). Owner: Omar Khan. Due: 2026-03-27.
- ACTION-4: Add a synthetic check that simulates KV-cache miss load to CI (low-freq) so we catch rebuild storms earlier. Owner: QA / Applied ML. Due: 2026-04-09.

Runbook TODO (explicit list to edit in Confluence)
- Add a new checklist section: 'When high p99 and OOMs coincide' (include commands above).
- Document the cache job naming conventions so runbook can identify warmup jobs by label.
- Create a quick rollback playbook for job canaries (one-liner CI rollback command).
- Add an alert runbook step: 'If mem > 85% and OOMs observed then scale down warmup concurrency or kill job'.

Open questions / unresolved
- Was this specific to canary tag only or to the warmup algorithm in general? need deploy logs + warmup job metrics. (Ping: @lena)
- Should we add a hard memory quota at the k8s pod level for warmup job? (Pros/cons tradeoff vs perf)
- Are there any customer-facing incidents tied to this window? I checked support queue; nothing flagged yet but double-check with CS.

Paging notes (for whoever takes next shift)
- If you see latency spike and dmesg OOMs: first step = scale up serving pool + rollback warmup job.
- Avoid immediate node reboots — prefer cordon + drain if host exhibits repeated OOM.
- If can't rollback (CI failure) -> trigger temporary routing policy: route 10% traffic to fallback-lite models (console -> routing -> apply policy).

Handoff checklist (what I did and what remains)
- [x] Incident contained and latency normalized.
- [x] Basic RCA notes captured here.
- [ ] File formal postmortem if Jira SRE-4123 is escalated to Sev2 (TBD). Owner: Omar/Incident lead.
- [ ] Runbook edits (see Runbook TODO). Owner: Omar + Samir.
- [ ] Confirm PR for warmup throttle lands and is merged. Owner: Lena.

Personal TODO (during shift)
- 09:00 PT: Ping CS to confirm no customer impact (Slack message drafted).
- 10:30 PT: Pair with Samir to sketch runbook edits (20–30m).
- 13:00 PT: Re-run synthetic KV rebuild test on staging.
- End of shift: tidy this doc, file short summary to #oncall-logs channel.

Misc notes
- Observed oddness: one host had swap thrashing even though swap is mostly disabled; need infra check on node kernel config. Add to infra triage.
- Suggestion for platform: add a 'job kill' circuit breaker that auto-stops particularly noisy jobs if mem/sched thresholds exceeded (must go through product/security review).

Links and refs (for handoff)
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.com/trace?id=abc123
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.com/query?range=1h&filter=svc-model-v2
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4123
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678

End of docket.
(Will update if anything new comes up before handoff at 15:45 PT)
